cohort: 563 neonates born to 556 mothers (7 twin pairs) who tested positive for COVID-19 between April 15, 2020, and September 15, 2021, at a level-3 teaching Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) in South India.
finding: Maternal COVID-19 status was not associated with increased risk of preterm birth, neonatal admission, morbidity, or mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was more common among COVID-19 positive mothers (73.5%) compared to COVID-19 negative mothers (P=.01), and rooming-in was less common among babies born to COVID-19 positive mothers (85.2%) compared to those born to COVID-19 negative mothers (94.6%, P=.02), but direct breastfeeding or rooming-in were not associated with increased risk of neonatal COVID-19 infection.
